From C+ to C++: Modernizing a GameBoy Emulator - Tom Tesch - CppCon 2025
---

After my CPPCON 2024 talk on writing the world’s fastest GameBoy emulator in Modern C++, several audience members reached out with emulators of their own. One stood out: a clean, test-driven implementation written in what its author jokingly called “C+” — describing it as C enhanced with C++’s std::vector. 
 
 In this follow-up talk, I’ll walk through the process of porting that implementation to modern C++, exploring how the language’s high-level constructs can affect both clarity and performance. This is not a rewrite for its own sake, but a pragmatic investigation into what modern C++ can offer in terms of speed, maintainability, and expressiveness — and whether we can do better than a minimal, well-crafted C-with-classes baseline. 
 
 I’ll also examine what it takes to make the codebase compatible with multithreaded execution, and reflect on the real-world trade-offs encountered
title: From C+ to C++: Modernizing a GameBoy Emulator - Tom Tesch - CppCon 2025
